title: The 2026 House push: Burlison, the June events and the select committee proposal
notes: Burlison's 2026 letters and events, the June 2026 Capitol events and the select-committee proposal; the FFRDC letters themselves sit with the FFRDC topic.

lead.text: Alongside the Oversight Committee's UAP hearings of 2023 to 2025, Rep. Eric Burlison named David Grusch a special adviser in March 2025, sent MITRE a records demand in May 2026, and saw the House adopt his UAP Disclosure Act amendment to the FY2027 NDAA in July 2026.

summary.text: By Burchett's press release and The Hill's reporting, the Congressional UAP Caucus was founded by Tim Burchett in August 2023 and counts Burlison, Moskowitz, Ogles and Luna among its members; its members' transparency and whistleblower bills have been filed and referred without advancing.
The Hill reported two requests for a House select committee on UAP: Burchett's under Speaker McCarthy, lost with McCarthy's speakership, and Burlison's in March 2024. None has been created.

As reported, and in Senator Mike Rounds's own newsletter, June 2026 brought three public events: a 9 June Capitol press conference hosted by the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets, a 25 June Disclosure Forum at which Burlison spoke, and a Disclosure Symposium where Rounds announced another UAP Disclosure Act amendment.

The House push ran beside an executive track: the President's February 2026 direction to release UAP files, the Department of War's PURSUE releases under Pete Hegseth, and a July 2026 directive on nondisclosure agreements.

record.text: Burlison named Grusch Special Advisor to his office on 27 March 2025, citing his NRO and NGA service and the credible-and-urgent whistleblower finding; the role expressly includes service on the Task Force on the Declassification of Federal Secrets.

At the 9 September 2025 hearing Burlison said his UAP disclosure amendment to the NDAA had been ruled non-germane, mostly by staff; that in 2024 someone in House administration had blocked a full AARO briefing; and that the UAP Disclosure Act had been stripped out by the House the year before.
At the same hearing Burlison played footage he described as an MQ-9 drone tracking an orb off Yemen on 30 October 2024 while another MQ-9 launched a Hellfire missile.

Burlison's letter to MITRE, dated 22 May 2026, runs to ten pages with over 40 production requests on UAP, anomalous materials and reverse engineering back to 1930, and asks for unclassified records within 45 days in native electronic format with complete metadata.

The House adopted Burlison's UAP Disclosure Act amendment to the FY2027 NDAA in July 2026. As reported by NewsTalk KZRG, it would have agencies identify, preserve and transfer UAP records to the National Archives on a statutory timeline, create an independent review board with Senate-confirmed members and subpoena authority, and reach contractors holding covered records.

In a 29 July 2026 press release Burlison said waiving UAP-related NDAs was something he had been calling for, offered his office's help to employees and contractors who wished to disclose, and recommended that they ask for a member of Congress and counsel to be present.

Burchett's H.R. 8424 of 16 May 2024 died in referral and was refiled as H.R. 1187 on 11 February 2025 with Moskowitz and Luna as cosponsors; his whistleblower bills H.R. 10111 and H.R. 5060 were likewise referred, and none of the four has advanced beyond referral.
On 1 April 2026 Luna wrote to Hegseth for video files held by AARO, after September 2025 witnesses told the Task Force that AARO held additional records.

The President stated on 19 February 2026 that he would direct the Secretary of War to begin identifying and releasing files; the Department's PURSUE programme published five releases between 8 May and 7 August 2026, and no executive order establishing it has been published.
A caucus is not a committee under 10 U.S.C. 119(g), and neither Burlison nor Luna holds a seat that carries any entitlement to notice of waived special access programmes.

claimed.text: Burlison told The Hill in March 2024 that a select committee would first question the Defense Department on spending he believes goes to secret UAP recovery programmes, that he had the support of Comer, Burchett and Moskowitz, and that the Department had not been transparent with members in a SCIF.

Burlison said in May 2026 that anything hidden from Congress would be handed to a private contractor, and named RAND, MITRE, Aerospace Corp, MIT Lincoln Labs and Northrop Grumman as the trail he was following. He has described, as his own inference, a programme organised from the FFRDC level.

At the 9 June 2026 Capitol event Luna said lawmakers were asking the White House to grant immunity to whistleblowers, Burlison called on the President to waive all NDAs and described a dead drop of information to his office, Grusch said political appointees had not complied with the disclosure law, and Moskowitz called for disclosure.

At the Task Force's Capitol press conference Grusch said he had found slush funds of billions of dollars a year, called it a fraud, waste and abuse issue, accused the Defense Intelligence Agency of obstructing oversight by withholding documents, and said the government is aware of several kinds of non-human intelligence. Burlison called for penalties for officials who withhold information from Congress.

At the 25 June 2026 Disclosure Forum Burlison announced that MIT Lincoln Laboratory had agreed to make available a 1952 recording, and the Disclosure Foundation's Jordan Flowers credited him: "He's stopped asking politely."

Hegseth told reporters in February 2026 that the Department would be in full compliance with what he called that executive order, and that he did not want to over-promise and under-deliver; Luna thanked the President for the direction as chair of the Task Force.

Fox News reported in July 2026 that the President directed the Department of War and the intelligence community to waive UAP-related NDAs for former employees and contractors speaking to authorised investigators, and that officials said it was not a declassification directive and permitted disclosure only to cleared investigators at AARO or the PURSUE task force.

Comer and Burlison opened a House Oversight probe into missing and dead scientists in April 2026 after the disappearance of Gen. William Neil McCasland; Burlison's staff had been trying to reach McCasland about a separate investigation before he vanished.

contested.text: No published instrument matches Hegseth's phrase that executive order; the board infers that either he described a social-media post as an order or an unpublished order exists.

Burlison said that The Aerospace Corporation sent two executives to a SCIF meeting with his office and that they knew nothing about UAP or reverse engineering; MITRE's spokesperson said only that any relevant material found would be handled with the responsible federal agencies.

On the board's reading the July 2026 NDA waiver frees witnesses only inside the executive channel run by the institution they would accuse, the structure Grusch used through the Inspector General before his career ended.
The records disagree on when the House adopted the amendment: one gives 22 July 2026, another 23 July, and the board carries the range rather than choosing.
The board infers that no UAP subpoena has issued from the Oversight Committee under Comer despite repeated member requests.

questions: Did MITRE produce anything responsive by the 45-day deadline in its letter?
What is the provenance and chain of custody of the MQ-9 footage Burlison played in September 2025?
Does Grusch's advisory role in Burlison's office carry a clearance or SCIF access?
Does any executive order text exist behind the February 2026 direction, and on which day in February did the direction and Hegseth's reference to it fall?
Why has no House select committee on UAP been created despite two attempts and the stated support of the Oversight chairman?
Will the Senate keep the House-adopted disclosure amendment, including its reach to contractors?
On what terms did Luna move from demanding AARO's abolition to endorsing its director?
Has anyone used Burlison's office, or the NDA waiver, to bring information forward?
